items.title: Fixed-design least squares as orthogonal projection
items.statement:
Let $n,d\in\mathbb N$ with $n,d\ge1$, and let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ be a fixed design
matrix, and write $V_X:=\{X\theta:\theta\in\mathbb R^d\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n$
for its column space. For an observed vector $y\in\mathbb R^n$, the **fixed-design
least-squares fitted vector** is

$$\widehat\mu_X(y):=P_{V_X}y,$$

where $P_{V_X}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $V_X$, as defined in
[[def-orthogonal-projection]]. It is uniquely defined even when $X$ is rank
deficient. The nearest-point characterization in
[[thm-orthogonal-projection-is-the-unique-nearest-point]] says that
$\widehat\mu_X(y)$ minimizes $\|y-v\|_2$ over $v\in V_X$. This item defines the
fitted vector; it does not select a coefficient representation $\widehat\theta$.

items.title: A binomial support-count bound
items.statement:
For $d,m\in\mathbb N$ with $1\le m\le d$,

$$\binom{d}{m}\le\left(\frac{ed}{m}\right)^m.$$

Here $\binom{d}{m}$ is the number of $m$-element subsets of a $d$-element set,
$m!$ is the factorial, $e=\exp(1)$, and integer powers have the convention of
[[def-integer-power]].

items.title: Finite-dimensional orthogonal projections are linear and contractive
items.statement:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, let $W\subseteq V$ be a
linear subspace, and let $P_W:V\to W$ be the orthogonal projection. Then $P_W$
is linear and satisfies $\|P_Wx\|\le \|x\|$ for every $x\in V$. In particular,
$P_W$ is continuous.

items.title: Finite tie-broken projection searches are Borel measurable
items.statement:
Let $n,N\ge1$ and let $P_1,\ldots,P_N$ be orthogonal projections in
$\mathbb R^n$ onto fixed finite-dimensional subspaces $V_1,\ldots,V_N$. Let
$c_1,\ldots,c_N\in\mathbb R$ be fixed. For $y\in\mathbb R^n$, define
$q_i(y):=n^{-1}\|y-P_i y\|_2^2+c_i$, choose the least index attaining
$\min_{1\le i\le N}q_i(y)$, and return its fitted vector $P_i y$. The resulting
map $\widehat m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n$ is Borel measurable. The index map
is Borel measurable when $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has its discrete sigma-algebra.

items.title: Isotropic Gaussian noise has the matching sub-Gaussian proxy
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge1$, $\sigma\ge0$, and let
$\varepsilon\sim N_n(0,\sigma^2I_n)$ be a centered multivariate normal vector.
Then for every $u\in\mathbb R^n$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb R$,
$$\mathbb E\exp(\lambda\langle u,\varepsilon\rangle) =\exp\!\left(\frac{\sigma^2\lambda^2\|u\|_2^2}{2}\right).$$
In particular, $\varepsilon$ is sub-Gaussian with proxy $\sigma^2$ in the
linear-functional sense of [[def-subgaussian-variable-and-vector]].

items.title: Penalized support-search least squares
items.statement:
**Input:** naturals $n,d\ge1$, a fixed design $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, a data
vector $y\in\mathbb R^n$, and a penalty $\tau^2\ge0$.

List all supports $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ in lexicographic order of their
length-$d$ indicator vectors, using $0<1$. For each $S$, let $V_S$ be the span
of the corresponding columns of $X$, compute $\widehat\mu_S=P_{V_S}y$, and
score

$$q_S:=n^{-1}\|y-\widehat\mu_S\|_2^2+\tau^2|S|.$$

Initialize the incumbent at the first support and scan the rest in order,
replacing it exactly when a strictly smaller score is found; on a tie retain the
earlier support. Return the selected support $\widehat S$ and fitted vector
$\widehat\mu_{\mathrm{BIC}}=\widehat\mu_{\widehat S}$. The candidate family is
finite by [[cor-cardinality-of-the-power-set]], and the fitted-vector selection
is Borel measurable by [[lem-finite-support-projection-selection-is-borel]].
This is an exhaustive combinatorial procedure, not an efficiency guarantee.

items.title: Constrained support-search least squares
items.statement:
**Input:** naturals $n,d\ge1$, a fixed design $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, a data
vector $y\in\mathbb R^n$, and a natural $s$ with $0\le s\le d$.

**Candidate supports:** list all subsets $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ with
$|S|\le s$ in lexicographic order of their length-$d$ indicator vectors,
using $0<1$. This is a finite nonempty list because it contains $\varnothing$
and is contained in the finite power set of $\{1,\ldots,d\}$.

**Procedure:** for each candidate $S$, let $V_S$ be the span of the columns of
$X$ indexed by $S$ and compute $\widehat\mu_S=P_{V_S}y$. Compute its residual
score $q_S=\|y-\widehat\mu_S\|_2^2$. Initialize the incumbent at the first
candidate. Scan the remaining candidates in the stated order, replacing the
incumbent exactly when a strictly smaller score is found; retain the earlier
candidate on a tie. Return the selected support and its fitted vector
$\widehat\mu_s$.

Each $V_S$ is finite-dimensional, so the projections are defined by
[[def-fixed-design-projection-estimator]]. The fitted-vector selection is Borel
measurable by [[lem-finite-support-projection-selection-is-borel]]. The procedure
performs a finite exhaustive support search; no computational-efficiency claim is
made.

items.title: Exact squared-error risk of an isotropic projection fit
items.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$, let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ be fixed, and put
$V=\operatorname{col}(X)$ and $r=\dim V$. Let $P_V$ be the orthogonal
projection and let $\mu\in\mathbb R^n$ be fixed. Let
$\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_n)$ be a centered random vector
with square-integrable coordinates satisfying
$\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i\varepsilon_j]=\sigma^2\mathbf 1_{i=j}$ for
$\sigma^2\ge0$. For $Y=\mu+\varepsilon$ and
$\widehat\mu=\widehat\mu_X(Y)$ as in
[[def-fixed-design-projection-estimator]],

$$\mathbb E\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2^2=\|P_V\mu-\mu\|_2^2+r\sigma^2.$$

In particular, when $\mu\in V$, the expected squared fitted-value error is
exactly $r\sigma^2$. The moment assumptions hold for centered Gaussian noise
with covariance matrix $\sigma^2 I_n$; Gaussianity is not otherwise needed.

items.title: Sub-Gaussian projection risk bounds
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a fixed subspace of dimension
$r$, and let $\mu\in V$. Suppose $Y=\mu+\varepsilon$, where
$\varepsilon\in\mathbb R^n$ is centered sub-Gaussian with proxy $\sigma^2\ge0$
in the linear-functional sense of
[[def-subgaussian-variable-and-vector]]. Put $\widehat\mu=P_VY$. Then
$\widehat\mu-\mu=P_V\varepsilon$.
If $r=0$ or $\sigma^2=0$, this error is zero almost surely. If $r\ge1$ and
$\sigma^2>0$, for every $t>0$,

$$\mathbb P\bigl(\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2^2>t\bigr)\le 2\cdot6^r\exp\!\left(-\frac{t}{8\sigma^2}\right).$$

Consequently, for every $0<\delta<1$,

$$\mathbb P\!\left(\frac1n\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2^2\le\frac{8\sigma^2}{n}\left[r\log6+\log\!\left(\frac2\delta\right)\right]\right)\ge1-\delta,$$

and

$$\mathbb E\left[\frac1n\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2^2\right]\le\frac{8\sigma^2}{n}\left(r\log6+\log2+\frac{13}{10}\right).$$
For $r\ge1$, both bounds are at most
$C\sigma^2(r+\log(1/\delta))/n$ and $C\sigma^2r/n$, respectively, for a
universal constant $C$. In the fixed-design model $Y=X\theta^*+\varepsilon$
with $\mu=X\theta^*\in\operatorname{col}(X)$, this is the fitted vector of
[[def-fixed-design-projection-estimator]].

items.title: BIC fitted-value risk bound
items.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$, let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ be fixed, and let
$\theta^*\in\mathbb R^d$ have a nonempty support
$S^*:=\{j:\theta_j^*\ne0\}$ of size $s:=|S^*|\ge1$. Suppose
$Y=X\theta^*+\varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R^n$ is centered
sub-Gaussian with proxy $\sigma^2\ge0$ in the linear-functional sense of
[[def-subgaussian-variable-and-vector]]. Run
[[alg-bic-penalized-least-squares]] with

$$\tau^2=16\log(6)\frac{\sigma^2}{n}+32\frac{\sigma^2\log(ed)}{n}.$$

For every admissible input to [[alg-bic-penalized-least-squares]], its finite
scan terminates and returns a support minimizing
$n^{-1}\|y-P_{V_S}y\|_2^2+\tau^2|S|$ over all supports. Among tied minimizers,
it returns the earliest support in the prescribed order.

Moreover, there is a universal constant
$C_0:=64+64\log6+32\log4$ such that, for every $0<\delta<1$,

$$\mathbb P\!\left(\frac1n\|\widehat\mu_{\mathrm{BIC}}-X\theta^*\|_2^2 \le C_0\frac{\sigma^2[s\log(ed)+\log(1/\delta)]}{n}\right)\ge1-\delta.$$

Since $s\ge1$, this also gives
$C_0\sigma^2s\log(ed/\delta)/n$. The theorem makes no design-rank,
incoherence, or column-normalization assumption. It asserts no zero right-hand
side when $s=0$.

items.title: Sparse constrained least-squares risk bound
items.statement:
For every admissible input to [[alg-constrained-l0-least-squares]], its finite
scan terminates and returns a support minimizing $\|y-P_{V_S}y\|_2^2$ over all
supports of size at most $s$. Among tied minimizers, it returns the earliest
support in the prescribed order.

Moreover, let $n,d$ be positive integers, let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ be fixed, and
let $\theta^*\in\mathbb R^d$ have at most $s$ nonzero coordinates, where
$1\le s\le d/2$. Suppose $Y=X\theta^*+\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon$ is centered
sub-Gaussian with proxy $\sigma^2\ge0$ in the linear-functional sense of
[[def-subgaussian-variable-and-vector]]. Let $\widehat\mu_s$ be the fitted vector
returned by [[alg-constrained-l0-least-squares]]. For $0<\delta<1$, with
$C:=32(4+2\log6)$,

$$\mathbb E\left[\frac1n\|\widehat\mu_s-X\theta^*\|_2^2\right] \le C\frac{\sigma^2s\log(ed/s)}{n},$$

and

$$\mathbb P\!\left(\frac1n\|\widehat\mu_s-X\theta^*\|_2^2 \le C\frac{\sigma^2\left[s\log(ed/s)+\log(1/\delta)\right]}{n}\right) \ge1-\delta.$$
No design-rank, incoherence, or column-normalization condition is assumed. The
claim concerns fitted values; it gives no coefficient-error bound.

items.title: Gaussian sparse-sequence minimax lower bound
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n,d\ge1$, $\sigma>0$, and let
$1\le s\le d/2$ be integers. Observe $Z\in\mathbb R^d$ with independent
coordinates $Z_j\sim N(\theta_j,\sigma^2/n)$ for a parameter
$$\Theta_{s,d}:=\{\theta\in\mathbb R^d: |\{j\in\{1,\ldots,d\}:\theta_j\ne0\}|\le s\}.$$
For every Borel estimator $T:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$,
$$\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{s,d}} \mathbb E_\theta\|T(Z)-\theta\|_2^2 \ge \frac{\sigma^2s\log(ed/s)}{200000n}.$$

items.title: Matching minimax rate in a Gaussian orthogonal sequence model
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n=d\ge2$, let $1\le s\le n/2$, and take
the fixed design $X=\sqrt n\,I_n$. For
$$\Theta_s:=\{\theta\in\mathbb R^n: |\{j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:\theta_j\ne0\}|\le s\},$$
observe $Y=X\theta+\varepsilon$ with one common noise law
$\varepsilon\sim N_n(0,\sigma^2I_n)$, where $\sigma>0$. For Borel fitted-vector
estimators $T:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n$, define
$$R^*_{n,s}:=\inf_{T\ \mathrm{Borel}}\ \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_s} \mathbb E_\theta\left[\frac1n\|T(Y)-X\theta\|_2^2\right].$$
Then for $C=32(4+2\log6)$,
$$\frac{\sigma^2s\log(en/s)}{200000n} \le R^*_{n,s} \le\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_s}\mathbb E_\theta\left[ \frac1n\|\widehat\mu_s(Y)-X\theta\|_2^2\right] \le C\frac{\sigma^2s\log(en/s)}n,$$
where $\widehat\mu_s$ is the constrained support-search fitted vector. Thus
this Gaussian orthogonal-sequence model has a matching minimax rate up to
universal constants. The sparse upper-bound theorem itself is choice-free; this corollary
assumes AC for its Gaussian law and Fano lower-bound suppliers.

items.title: Collinear columns identify a fitted mean, not its coefficients
items.statement:
For every fixed-design matrix $X$, the map $\theta\mapsto X\theta$ is injective;
therefore the coefficient vector is determined by its fitted mean.

items.title: Constrained least squares in a two-coordinate orthogonal sequence model
items.statement:
Let $n=d=2$, $X=I_2$, $\theta^*=0$, and impose sparsity $s=1$. Observe
$Y=X\theta^*+\varepsilon=\varepsilon$. Assume the
centered noise vector is sub-Gaussian with proxy $\sigma^2>0$ and has covariance
$\sigma^2 I_2$. The constrained support search retains the coordinate with the
larger squared observation. Its expected fitted-value error per observation is
between $\sigma^2/2$ and $\sigma^2$, and the general theorem gives the upper
bound $C\sigma^2\log(2e)/2$.

items.title: Zero training residual and positive test error
items.statement:
Take one fixed-design observation with $X=[1]$, true fitted mean $\mu=0$, and
training response $Y=\varepsilon$. Let $\varepsilon'$ be an independent fresh
response error with the same mean-zero, variance-$\sigma^2$ law, where
$\sigma^2>0$. Least squares fits the one-dimensional column space exactly: its
training residual is zero, its expected error for estimating the mean is
$\sigma^2$, and its expected squared error for predicting the fresh response is
$2\sigma^2$.
